value.summary: On rack R01, cable C05 was not fully clicked in, so the tech reseated it by hand and the link came up.
On rack R01, the connector at C31 was not latched, the second such case today.
On rack R01, the robot landed cable F22 in port FE-LEAF2/5 instead of FE-LEAF2/4, and it was moved to the correct port.
On rack R02, the robot had a gripper fault on cable C27 and stopped after three retries, and the tech finished the connection by hand.
On rack R04, the robot's gripper dropped an RJ45 cable for C19 under the tray, and the tech retrieved it and plugged it in by hand.
On rack R01, the label on cable C40 read M2 while the port map said M1, and the tech printed a new label.
While routing cable C12 on rack R01, the robot arm caught the neighboring BMC cable, which was already up, and pulled it half out; the tech reseated it and the link came back after about 30 seconds.
On rack R09, the robot took about 4 minutes to complete cable C47 as the arm kept re-planning around the bundle, but it finished without the tech stepping in.
On rack R06, the robot's camera lost track of port F31 twice under the aisle LEDs, and the third attempt succeeded.
On rack R05, the F28 cable carried a tag printed for port P1 while the cable was on port P2, and the tech swapped the tags.
On rack R01, the fiber end face at F03 failed scope inspection, was cleaned, and passed a second inspection.
On rack R01, fiber F17 had dust on the ferrule, and the tech noted these jumpers came out of the bag without caps.
On rack R02, the cable for F09 had a kinked jacket right behind the connector, and the tech swapped in a new jumper from spares.
The cable kit for rack R03 was missing two copper patch cords, which were replaced from spares with a 15-minute wait.
The rear door of rack R06 was locked, and the tech waited 20 minutes for a security badge.
A laptop cart left in the aisle blocked the robot at rack R08, and it waited about 4 minutes until the cart was moved, with nobody near it.
On rack R05, the cord for C33 was 0.5 m long but needs to be 1 m to reach the management switch without strain.
On rack R06, cable F14 arrived out of the bundle bent past its bend radius near the boot.
Tray 9 was not yet installed in rack R08 when the robot arrived, so it skipped those slots and returned to complete them after the tray was installed.
Cable F30 on rack R02 had no link because the port map had P1 and P2 swapped for tray 15; the network team corrected the map and the robot re-ran the connection.
On rack R08, the leaf switch port for F35 was administratively down; the network team enabled it and the link came up.
At shift start on rack R03, the MGMT-SW2 uplink was not yet patched, and the network team finished it before the robot reached those ports.
On rack R04, the port map revision on the tablet (rev C) and on the rack sheet (rev D) disagreed for FE-LEAF2, so the fiber was held until the network team confirmed rev D.
A contractor walked into the aisle behind rack R02 while the robot arm was extended; the robot froze within a second and resumed once he left, with no contact.
At rack R03, the robot arm swung toward a technician's hand as they reached in to clear a zip tie; the technician pressed the e-stop, and the arm came close but did not touch them.
At rack R04, the robot pinched a technician's glove on the fiber tray door while the technician was holding it open; there was no injury and the glove was not damaged.
An electrician working on the PDU in this row pressed the stop as a precaution while he opened the panel, not because of anything the robot did.
On shift 9 at rack R09, the tech noted something was off with the fiber and referred questions to Dana.
On rack R11 during shift 11, a few ports were flapping in the afternoon, and the tech was not sure whether the robot work or the switch was the cause.
On shift 13 at rack R13, the tech stepped in and referred to a photo without describing what happened.
